title: Tamagotchi Virtual Pet
summary: Egg-shaped keychain virtual pet device created in Japan by Aki Maita and Akihiro Yokoi, requiring users to feed, clean, and care for a digital creature.
facts: Released by Bandai in Japan in November 1996 and worldwide in May 1997.
Sold over 80 million units worldwide during its peak popularity.
Spurred school bans due to constant feeding and attention alarms.

title: Ty Beanie Babies
summary: Line of plush stuffed animals filled with plastic pellets ('beans') created by Ty Warner, sparking a speculative secondary market collector craze.
facts: Introduced Ty heart-shaped swing tags with custom poems and birth dates.
Ty Warner pioneered artificial scarcity by retiring specific designs without notice.
Early adopters traded rare Beanie Babies for thousands of dollars on early web auction sites like eBay.

title: Blockbuster Video
summary: Dominant home video and game rental retail chain featuring signature blue-and-yellow store design, VHS tape walls, and quick drop boxes.
facts: Operated over 9,000 stores worldwide at its peak in the late 1990s.
Famous tagline: 'Make it a Blockbuster Night'.
Pioneered revenue-sharing arrangements with major Hollywood movie studios.

title: Nike Air Max 95 & Air Jordan XI
summary: Iconic athletic footwear releases designed by Sergio Lozano (Air Max 95) and Tinker Hatfield (Air Jordan XI), defining 90s sneakerhead culture.
facts: Air Max 95 featured visible forefoot air cushioning and human anatomy-inspired layered upper.
Air Jordan XI introduced shiny patent leather and carbon fiber shank plates to basketball performance shoes.
Worn by Michael Jordan during the Chicago Bulls' legendary 72-10 1995-96 NBA championship season.

title: Nintendo Game Boy Pocket & Color
summary: Redesigned compact monochrome (Pocket) and color-display (Color) handheld gaming consoles created under Gunpei Yokoi's legacy.
facts: Game Boy Pocket (1996) reduced unit size by 30% and operated on two AAA batteries.
Game Boy Color (1998) introduced a crisp color LCD screen and backwards compatibility with all original Game Boy cartridges.
Fueled by the immense popularity of Pokémon Red, Blue, and Yellow games.
